candidates.text: Each team manages its own budget and inserts its own budget transactions.
candidates.rationale: The IFA only monitors and controls the balance; teams are responsible for managing their budgets.

candidates.text: The IFA can specify budget policies and the system must alert when violations occur.
candidates.rationale: The IFA sets regulation rules and needs the system to detect and alert on policy violations.

candidates.text: The IFA administrative can view all transactions across teams.
candidates.rationale: The IFA needs visibility into all monetary transactions for auditing and monitoring.

candidates.text: Referees must be able to insert game events in real time using a mobile device.
candidates.rationale: Referees need to record events like goals, offsides, red cards during the game for reliability.

candidates.text: Only the referee can update game events to ensure data reliability.
candidates.rationale: To maintain official and coherent data, only referees should input game events.

candidates.text: Each game event must include a timestamp, event type, and additional information.
candidates.rationale: Events need to be detailed with time and context for accurate records.

candidates.text: Game-related data (not budget) must be publicly accessible even to unregistered guests.
candidates.rationale: The system aims for transparency, allowing anyone to view game results and statistics.

candidates.text: The system must allow exporting of game data for journalists and press.
candidates.rationale: The requirement to export data was confirmed as needed for external reporting.

candidates.text: Team managers and administration can view and query their own team data for offline analysis.
candidates.rationale: Teams need access to their resources (players, coaches, budget) to perform analysis.

candidates.text: Each team can only access its own financial data; IFA can only view but not modify it.
candidates.rationale: Data ownership is per team; IFA monitors but cannot alter transactions.

candidates.text: The system must automatically schedule matches based on configurable policies (e.g., home/away, minimum gap).
candidates.rationale: Manual scheduling is replaced by an algorithm that respects defined constraints.

candidates.text: The system must allow definition of referee allocation policies (e.g., avoid same referee for same teams, equal game count).
candidates.rationale: Referee assignments need to be guided by fair policies to avoid bias.

candidates.text: Referees can submit their preferences (e.g., vacation days) which the scheduling algorithm must consider.
candidates.rationale: To accommodate referee availability, the system should incorporate their constraints.

candidates.text: Schedules can be manually overridden by an IFA representative with a documented rationale and approval.
candidates.rationale: Changes due to cancellations or issues require transparency and dual approval.

candidates.text: Fans can subscribe to specific games, teams, or players to receive push notifications.
candidates.rationale: Fans should get proactive updates on events they care about to improve engagement.

candidates.text: The system must support a fan portal with live updates from referees and live scores.
candidates.rationale: Fans need to see real-time game events and tournament standings.

candidates.text: Players can update their social network page within the system to communicate with fans.
candidates.rationale: Players need a channel to post messages and interact with fans.

candidates.text: The system must support user registration and profiles for all stakeholders (IFA, teams, referees, fans, players).
candidates.rationale: Identification is required for system access; guests can view only public data.

candidates.text: The system must include a process for team registration where IFA approves new teams.
candidates.rationale: Teams need to be officially registered with valid documents before managing resources.

candidates.text: The system must allow the IFA to define leagues, seasons, and register referees.
candidates.rationale: Basic system setup includes league and season definition and referee onboarding.

candidates.text: All historical data (schedules, events) must be archived for future analysis.
candidates.rationale: Archives support reasoning for gambling, future predictions, and record keeping.

candidates.text: The system must handle up to 50,000 concurrent users with reasonable response time (1-2 seconds for most users).
candidates.rationale: Scalability and performance are required to support large fan base and simultaneous access.

candidates.text: Referee mobile application must have real-time responsiveness with priority over other activities.
candidates.rationale: During games, referee input must be immediate to ensure live updates.

candidates.text: The system must be a unified system with different interfaces for different stakeholders (web for IFA/teams, mobile for referees/fans).
candidates.rationale: Different user groups need tailored interfaces but share the same backend.

candidates.text: The system must support localization (language, currency, timezone) and comply with local data regulations (e.g., German data must stay in Germany).
candidates.rationale: Global reach requires adaptation to local laws and user preferences.

candidates.text: Budget data must be encrypted to prevent leakage.
candidates.rationale: Financial data is sensitive and needs protection against unauthorized access.

candidates.text: The system should be developed and maintained by an external company, with IFA IT department overseeing communication.
candidates.rationale: IFA is not a software company and prefers outsourcing development and maintenance.
